sentences.en: Hello everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: I am here with some exceedingly exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我带来了一些极其令人兴奋的消息。

sentences.en: Now, as all our beloved club members will already know, one of the very best things of being a member of the Rest is History
sentences.zh: 现在，正如我们所有亲爱的俱乐部成员所知，成为“历史余韵”俱乐部成员最棒的事情之一，

sentences.en: Club is getting access to exclusive members-only miniseries.
sentences.zh: 就是可以收听独家的会员专享迷你剧集。

sentences.en: That's right, miniseries, not just individual episodes.
sentences.zh: 没错，是迷你剧集，不仅仅是单集节目。

sentences.en: So these are special episodes every other month, which only club members can listen to, no one else.
sentences.zh: 这些是每隔一个月推出的特别节目，只有俱乐部成员才能收听，其他人不行。

sentences.en: And we've got a brand new one coming out this February.
sentences.zh: 我们今年二月将推出一部全新的迷你剧集。

sentences.en: So that's going to be the very first one of 2026.
sentences.zh: 这将是 2026 年的第一部。

sentences.en: And it is presented by me and the great art critic
sentences.zh: 它将由我和伟大的艺术评论家

sentences.en: Laura Cumming.
sentences.zh: 劳拉·卡明共同呈现。

sentences.en: Four episodes.
sentences.zh: 共四集。

sentences.en: And it's about paintings that shed a particularly fascinating light on history.
sentences.zh: 内容是关于那些以极其迷人的视角阐释历史的画作。

sentences.en: And it covers a broad range of times and places.
sentences.zh: 它涵盖了广泛的时间和地点。

sentences.en: So everything from Velázquez is Las Meninas, described by many critics as the greatest of all paintings, right the way up to
sentences.zh: 从委拉斯开兹的《宫娥》——许多评论家称其为有史以来最伟大的画作——一直到

sentences.en: Henry Rayburn's Skating Minister.
sentences.zh: 亨利·雷伯恩的《滑冰的牧师》。

sentences.en: What do these paintings tell us about the times in which they were painted?
sentences.zh: 这些画作向我们揭示了它们创作时代怎样的信息？

sentences.en: It's really, really fascinating stuff.
sentences.zh: 内容真的非常、非常迷人。

sentences.en: And members will get a new one of those episodes every Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 会员们每周三都会收到其中一集新节目。

sentences.en: And it is starting this week on the 4th of February.
sentences.zh: 本周三，也就是 2 月 4 日就开始了。

sentences.en: So that's the Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 就是周三那天。

sentences.en: And if you are not watching it on YouTube or Spotify, if you're just listening to it as a
sentences.zh: 如果你不是在 YouTube 或 Spotify 上观看，而只是把它当作

sentences.en: podcast, don't worry, because we will be sending all our members an email, which will be going into
sentences.zh: 播客来收听，也不用担心，因为我们会给所有会员发送一封电子邮件，里面会

sentences.en: greater written detail about the painting, but also obviously giving you an image of the painting itself.
sentences.zh: 详细介绍画作的文字内容，当然也会附上画作本身的图片。

sentences.en: So you can have a quick look at that, perhaps before you listen to the episode.
sentences.zh: 这样你在收听节目之前，或许可以先快速浏览一下。

sentences.en: Although I have to say that Laura's descriptions of each painting are so good that perhaps you don't even need to look at the painting.
sentences.zh: 尽管我必须说，劳拉对每幅画的描述都非常精彩，以至于你可能根本不需要看画。

sentences.en: So if you would like to sign up to that mini-series and to the other five mini-series that we will be doing this year, which will be covering everything from
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想订阅这部迷你剧集，以及我们今年将制作的其他五部迷你剧集——内容涵盖从

sentences.en: history's greatest photographs, the Vietnam War, to England's she-wolves, then you know where to go.
sentences.zh: 历史上最伟大的照片、越南战争，到英国的“母狼”女王——你知道该去哪里。

sentences.en: Go to therestishistory.com if you are not already a club member and sign up there.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是俱乐部成员，请前往 therestishistory.com 注册。

sentences.en: Massinissa had already heard a great deal about Scipio's prowess as a general and hugely admired him.
sentences.zh: 马西尼萨早就听说过西庇阿作为将军的非凡才能，并对他极为钦佩。

sentences.en: The Numidian had formed a picture of the Roman in his mind's eye as a man of powerful and striking physique, but when at last he came face to face with Scipio, he was awestruck.
sentences.zh: 这位努米底亚人在脑海中勾勒出的罗马人形象，是一位体格强健、引人注目的男子，但当他最终与西庇阿面对面时，他被震撼了。

sentences.en: For in the flesh, the Roman general was even more impressive than he had been in Massinissa's imaginings.
sentences.zh: 因为现实中的这位罗马将军，比马西尼萨想象中还要令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Naturally possessed of great dignity, Scipio also, thanks to his longer hair, got a most graceful figure.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿天生具有威严，而且由于留着长发，他的身姿显得格外优雅。

sentences.en: This, however, owed nothing to any effeminate fussing over fashion or personal grooming, but rather to an appearance and bearing that was virile in the extreme,
sentences.zh: 然而，这并非源于任何女性化的时尚或个人修饰，而是一种极其阳刚的外表和风度，

sentences.en: for he was the very model of a warrior.
sentences.zh: 因为他简直就是战士的典范。

sentences.en: Scipio was just at the age when his physical powers were at full strength.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿正值体力巅峰的年纪。

sentences.en: And even though he had recently been ill, he had quite recaptured his youthful bloom.
sentences.zh: 尽管他最近生过病，但他已经完全恢复了青春活力。

sentences.en: Indeed, he seemed more handsome than ever.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他看起来比以往任何时候都更英俊。

sentences.en: So that was Rob Brydon describing one of history's more homoerotic summit meetings.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是罗伯·布莱顿在描述历史上一次更具同性情调的峰会。

sentences.en: Actually, it was the Italian-born Roman historian, Livy.
sentences.zh: 实际上，那是出生于意大利的罗马历史学家李维。

sentences.en: So that was your Roman accent, was it?
sentences.zh: 所以那是你的罗马口音，对吧？

sentences.en: That was the accent of an Italian, but actually, as it went on, it degenerated into the accent of an Italian who had set up an ice cream parlour in Swansea in the 1910s.
sentences.zh: 那是意大利人的口音，但实际上，随着讲述的深入，它退化成了 1910 年代在斯旺西开冰淇淋店的意大利人的口音。

sentences.en: Dominic, you and Welsh history, we just can't stop you doing it.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你和威尔士历史，我们真是拦不住你讲这个。

sentences.en: It's great to have some Welsh history back on the show.
sentences.zh: 节目里能重新出现威尔士历史真是太好了。

sentences.en: So that was the Roman historian, Livy, and he's describing this exciting meeting in 206 BC.
sentences.zh: 刚才那是罗马历史学家李维，他正在描述公元前 206 年那次激动人心的会面。

sentences.en: We are on the Atlantic coast of Iberia, now Spain, and the participants are two extremely strapping, well-oiled and handsome warlords.
sentences.zh: 我们现在位于伊比利亚（即现在的西班牙）的大西洋沿岸，参与者是两位极其强壮、油光水滑且英俊的军阀。

sentences.en: One of them is Masinissa, who is a Berber prince from modern-day Algeria, Numidia, as it then was.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是马西尼萨，他是来自现代阿尔及利亚（当时的努米底亚）的柏柏尔王子。

sentences.en: And the other is Publius Cornelius Scipio, who is a Roman patrician, a young man whom we met in our previous episode.
sentences.zh: 另一位是普布利乌斯·科尔内利乌斯·西庇阿，一位罗马贵族，我们在上一集里见过这位年轻人。

sentences.en: And Scipio, listeners may recall, was the officer whom, ten years before this meeting, had rallied
sentences.zh: 听众们可能还记得，西庇阿就是那位在这次会面十年前，在罗马遭遇坎尼战役惨败后，

sentences.en: the men of Rome in the wake of their shattering defeat at Cannae, and he had made them swear
sentences.zh: 召集了罗马人并让他们发誓

sentences.en: never to desert our country, nor to permit any other citizen of Rome to leave her in the lurch.
sentences.zh: 绝不背弃祖国，也不允许任何其他罗马公民抛弃祖国的人。

sentences.en: So, ten years on, here he is meeting this oiled warlord.
sentences.zh: 所以，十年过去了，他在这里会见了这位涂了油的军阀。

sentences.en: Tom, explain what's going on.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，解释一下发生了什么。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, extraordinary way of accents, for starters.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，首先，这口音真是太离谱了。

sentences.en: But there are some other puzzles as well.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他一些令人困惑的地方。

sentences.en: So, first of all, attentive listeners may be wondering, what is a Numidian doing meeting up with a Roman?
sentences.zh: 首先，细心的听众可能想问，一个努米底亚人为什么要和罗马人见面？

sentences.en: Because people who've listened to our previous episodes in this ongoing series will recall that the Numidians are the allies not of Rome, but of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 因为听过我们这个系列节目之前几集的听众会记得，努米底亚人不是罗马的盟友，而是迦太基的盟友。

sentences.en: And in fact, they are key allies because they are the best light cavalry in the world.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们是关键盟友，因为他们是世界上最优秀的轻骑兵。

sentences.en: They ride bareback, they don't bother with reins, they have spears and all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他们骑马不配马鞍，不用缰绳，装备着长矛和各种武器。

sentences.en: And they are the horsemen who have provided
sentences.zh: 他们就是那些为

sentences.en: Hannibal effectively with the cutting edge throughout his invasion of Italy and his occupation of Italy.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔在入侵和占领意大利期间提供了实质性尖端战力的骑兵。

sentences.en: And the Romans have learned to dread the Numidians possibly more than any other of the units in Hannibal's army.
sentences.zh: 罗马人对努米底亚人的恐惧，可能超过了汉尼拔军队中的任何其他部队。

sentences.en: So, what is going on here?
sentences.zh: 那么，这里到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: And secondly, what on earth is up with Scipio?
sentences.zh: 其次，西庇阿到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Because, Dominic, you read this kind of stern, traditionalist statement of Roman pluck and determination.
sentences.zh: 因为，多米尼克，你读的那段话是关于罗马人勇气和决心的严厉、传统的陈述。

sentences.en: I mean, Scipio is only 19 when he's saying that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，西庇阿说那番话时才 19 岁。

sentences.en: So, he's very callow, but it's very, very old school.
sentences.zh: 所以，他虽然很稚嫩，但非常、非常守旧。

sentences.en: I mean, it's patriotic in exactly the way that Roman
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这正是罗马

sentences.en: traditionalists expect young men to be patriotic.
sentences.zh: 传统主义者期望年轻人所表现出的那种爱国主义。

sentences.en: But something has changed and something very, very sinister.
sentences.zh: 但有些事情变了，而且是非常、非常阴险的变化。

sentences.en: If you recall the people who were paying attention to that reading and frankly, who wasn't, Scipio now has long hair, the most un-Roman thing imaginable.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得刚才那段朗读的内容——坦白说，谁没注意听呢——西庇阿现在留着长发，这是最不“罗马”的事情了。

sentences.en: So, is he like you going to India on your gap year?
sentences.zh: 所以，他是不是像你一样，间隔年去印度旅行了？

sentences.en: Is that what's going on?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, someone else who went to India, of course, is Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，还有一个人也去过印度，那就是亚历山大大帝。

sentences.en: And there's a definite hint of Alexander there.
sentences.zh: 而且这其中确实有亚历山大的影子。

sentences.en: And what is also a hint of Alexander is the fact that, according to Pliny the Elder, admittedly writing centuries later,
sentences.zh: 同样有亚历山大影子的是，根据老普林尼的记载——虽然他是在几个世纪后写的，

sentences.en: but I think we can rely on him, Scipio was the first Roman to shave daily.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们可以信赖他——西庇阿是第一个每天刮胡子的罗马人。

sentences.en: So, up until that point,
sentences.zh: 所以，在那之前，

sentences.en: Romans had generally been bearded.
sentences.zh: 罗马人通常都是留胡子的。

sentences.en: But now, Scipio has introduced this fashion for a clean chin.
sentences.zh: 但现在，西庇阿引领了这种刮净下巴的时尚。

sentences.en: And that, again, of course, is very, very Alexander.
sentences.zh: 而这，当然，也非常、非常“亚历山大”。

sentences.en: And when you think of that description, that passage that you read, the sense of awe that Masinissa feels at seeing this kind of divine, godlike figure, I mean, it's quite Homeric.
sentences.zh: 当你想到那段你读过的描述，想到马西尼萨看到这种神圣、如神般的人物时感到的敬畏，我的意思是，这非常有荷马史诗的味道。

sentences.en: It's the way that people are described in the Iliad, for instance, seeing Achilles.
sentences.zh: 就像《伊利亚特》中人们看到阿喀琉斯时的那种描写。

sentences.en: So, all in all, Scipio is cutting, for Roman traditionalists, it's a disturbingly kind of Greek dash.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，对于罗马传统主义者来说，西庇阿展现出了一种令人不安的希腊式风采。

sentences.en: Because Roman commanders are supposed to be old and craggy and bearded and all of that.
sentences.zh: 因为罗马指挥官本应是老成、粗犷、留着胡子的那种人。

sentences.en: And they are not supposed to look like Achilles.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该看起来像阿喀琉斯。

sentences.en: They are not supposed to look like Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该看起来像亚历山大大帝。

sentences.en: So, something odd is absolutely going on here.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里绝对发生了一些奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: So, when Livy is describing Scipio, there is a sense here, isn't there, that Scipio is more than an ordinary Roman general, as you've described, really.
sentences.zh: 那么，当李维描述西庇阿时，确实有一种感觉，即西庇阿不仅仅是一位普通的罗马将军，正如你所描述的那样。

sentences.en: This business about Alexander the Great, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如关于亚历山大大帝的这件事。

sentences.en: There is a sense, isn't there, in Livy's description that Scipio is, he's marketing himself as something actually quite old-fashioned, as a Greek-style, as indeed a Homeric hero,
sentences.zh: 在李维的描述中，确实有一种感觉，西庇阿在将自己包装成一种非常老派的形象，一种希腊式的，甚至就是荷马史诗英雄式的形象，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Somebody who has been appointed by the gods to lead the Romans back from the abyss of Cannae and Lake Trasimene and all the defeats that Hannibal has inflicted on them.
sentences.zh: 一个被神灵指派，带领罗马人从坎尼、特拉西梅诺湖以及汉尼拔给他们带来的所有失败的深渊中走出来的人。

sentences.en: And do you think this is a conscious thing?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是他有意识的行为吗？

sentences.en: And do you think Livy is genuinely reporting Scipio's PR strategy, as it were?
sentences.zh: 你认为李维是在真实地记录西庇阿的公关策略吗？

sentences.en: This is how Livy puts it.
sentences.zh: 李维是这样表述的。

sentences.en: He absolutely says it's a PR strategy.
sentences.zh: 他明确表示这就是一种公关策略。

sentences.en: So, to quote Livy, from Scipio's earliest days, he used to present his policies and actions as inspired by dreams or by warnings from heaven.
sentences.zh: 引用李维的话，西庇阿从很早开始，就习惯于将自己的政策和行动宣称为受到梦境或来自天堂的警告的启发。

sentences.en: And this is very ostentatiously performative.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常显眼的表演。

sentences.en: So, Livy tells us that
sentences.zh: 李维告诉我们，

sentences.en: Scipio, before he takes any course of action, he will go up to the capital, very obviously, and sit in the temple of Jupiter, as though he is communing with the god.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿在采取任何行动之前，都会非常显眼地前往卡皮托利诺山，坐在朱庇特神庙里，仿佛在与神灵交流。

sentences.en: And this, in turn, fosters what Livy describes as a very empty and foolish story, once told of Alexander the Great,
sentences.zh: 而这反过来又助长了李维所描述的那个关于亚历山大大帝的、非常空洞且愚蠢的故事，

sentences.en: that Scipio had been born from the embraces of a giant serpent, a monster that had often visited
sentences.zh: 即西庇阿是由一条巨蛇的拥抱所生，那怪物经常造访

sentences.en: his mother in her bedroom, but had always glided away and vanished the moment someone came in.
sentences.zh: 他母亲的卧室，但一旦有人进来，它就会滑走并消失。

sentences.en: I mean, sceptics may say, well, there's absolutely no evidence for this at all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，怀疑论者可能会说，好吧，这根本没有任何证据。

sentences.en: But clearly, what Scipio is doing is trying to imply that the serpent might have been Jupiter.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，西庇阿这样做是想暗示那条蛇可能就是朱庇特。

sentences.en: Because, of course, Dominic, you will remember that very similar stories were told of Alexander, that Jupiter had come in the form of a snake to Alexander's mother.
sentences.zh: 因为，多米尼克，你肯定记得关于亚历山大也有非常相似的故事，说朱庇特曾化身为蛇来到亚历山大的母亲身边。

sentences.en: So, Scipio obviously doesn't deny these stories, does he?
sentences.zh: 所以，西庇阿显然没有否认这些故事，对吧？

sentences.en: Why would he?
sentences.zh: 他为什么要否认呢？

sentences.en: As Livy says in his account, whether he was truly so superstitious as to believe this nonsense, or whether he fostered reports of it so that people would obey him the
sentences.zh: 正如李维在叙述中所说，他到底是真迷信到相信这些无稽之谈，还是为了让人们更服从他而故意散布这些传闻，

sentences.en: more, is unclear.
sentences.zh: 这并不清楚。

sentences.en: So, Scipio just lets the stories kind of build and build.
sentences.zh: 所以，西庇阿只是任由这些故事不断发酵。

sentences.en: Now, I guess Scipio knows that what the Romans are craving is, well, at first, what they were craving was a figure of reassurance, right?
sentences.zh: 我想西庇阿知道罗马人渴望的是什么，嗯，起初，他们渴望的是一个能带来安慰的人物，对吧？

sentences.en: A conservative figure, a memory of Roman virtues paSt. But he's changing, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 一个保守的人物，一个对过去罗马美德的记忆。但他正在改变，不是吗？

sentences.en: And he's developing a new strategy to sort of impress his personality on the Roman masses.
sentences.zh: 他正在制定一种新的策略，将自己的个性强加给罗马大众。

sentences.en: And he's becoming, I dare, I mean, Tom, you have compared him in your notes to a rock star.
sentences.zh: 他正在变成，我敢说，汤姆，你在笔记中把他比作摇滚明星。

sentences.en: He's turning himself into a figure of kind of rock star glamour and charisma.
sentences.zh: 他正在把自己变成一个具有摇滚明星般魅力和光环的人物。

sentences.en: He's very good looking, he's very suave, and he's kind of promoting himself as possibly as the son of a god.
sentences.zh: 他长得很帅，举止优雅，而且他正在把自己宣传为可能是神的儿子。

sentences.en: And of course, he is in a republic.
sentences.zh: 当然，他身处一个共和国。

sentences.en: And republics don't tend to look favourably on kind of rock stars posing as the son of a god.
sentences.zh: 而共和国通常不太喜欢那种自诩为神之子的“摇滚明星”。

sentences.en: So, there must be some people who think this guy's a terrible person.
sentences.zh: 所以，肯定有一些人认为这家伙是个糟糕透顶的人。

sentences.en: I mean, this is, that he's showy and brash.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他爱炫耀且轻浮。

sentences.en: And I mean, this is actually a complaint that people will level at lots of Roman figures to come, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且，这实际上是人们后来对许多罗马人物提出的抱怨，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But Scipio is establishing a brand that, as you say, many Romans to come will copy well into the period when the republic has actually collapsed and been replaced by an empire.
sentences.zh: 但西庇阿建立了一个品牌，正如你所说，许多后来的罗马人会效仿，一直持续到共和国实际上已经崩溃并被帝国取代的时期。

sentences.en: But Scipio is blazing the path for, you know, these kind of younger, showboating emperors who will appear.
sentences.zh: 但西庇阿为那些后来出现的年轻、爱炫耀的皇帝开辟了道路。

sentences.en: But Scipio is going to end up, so a lot of people listening to this may already know,
sentences.zh: 但西庇阿最终会，很多听众可能已经知道了，

sentences.en: Scipio is going to end up as the great antagonist of Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿最终会成为汉尼拔的头号宿敌。

sentences.en: The two of them are kind of linked in the imagination for people who study the classical world.
sentences.zh: 对于研究古典世界的人来说，他们两人在想象中是紧密相连的。

sentences.en: And their encounter, their duel, will become the great turning point in the Punic Wars.
sentences.zh: 他们的相遇，他们的决斗，将成为布匿战争的伟大转折点。

sentences.en: And Scipio gives the Romans the one thing they've craved all this time, which is their own figure with the glamour, the charisma and the
sentences.zh: 西庇阿给了罗马人他们一直渴望的一样东西，那就是他们自己拥有汉尼拔那种魅力、感召力以及

sentences.en: effectiveness, the military effectiveness of Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 军事效能的人物。

sentences.en: Now, actually, Hannibal is relatively well-born, isn't he, in Carthaginian terMs. And Scipio is also extremely well-born.
sentences.zh: 现在，实际上，汉尼拔的出身相对高贵，不是吗，以迦太基的标准来看。而西庇阿的出身也极其高贵。

sentences.en: I mean, he is positively posh.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他非常时髦。

sentences.en: He went to Harrow.
sentences.zh: 他上过哈罗公学。

sentences.en: Christchurch.
sentences.zh: 基督堂学院。

sentences.en: Maybe Christchurch or did he go to
sentences.zh: 也许是基督堂学院，还是他去了

sentences.en: Durham?
sentences.zh: 达勒姆？

sentences.en: No, he went to Christchurch because he, I mean, he's the poshest of the posh and he's very smart.
sentences.zh: 不，他去了基督堂学院，因为他，我的意思是，他是贵族中的贵族，而且非常聪明。

sentences.en: He's very charismatic.
sentences.zh: 他非常有魅力。

sentences.en: I mean, he's got it all because he is a patrician.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他拥有一切，因为他是一位贵族。

sentences.en: So he is from one of the ancient aristocratic dynasties of Rome.
sentences.zh: 所以他来自罗马古老的贵族王朝之一。

sentences.en: But having said that, actually, the Scipios have only recently come into political prominence.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，实际上，西庇阿家族只是最近才在政治上崭露头角。

sentences.en: And basically, the Punic Wars has been the making of the Scipios and their reputation.
sentences.zh: 基本上，布匿战争成就了西庇阿家族及其声誉。

sentences.en: So back in the first Punic War, two of them had done well enough to be awarded triumphs.
sentences.zh: 早在第一次布匿战争中，他们家族中就有两人表现出色，获得了凯旋式。

sentences.en: Scipio's uncle is called Calvus.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿的叔叔叫卡尔武斯。

sentences.en: He's nicknamed Calvus, which means baldy.
sentences.zh: 他的绰号是卡尔武斯，意思是“秃头”。

sentences.en: He had been consul in 222 and was a great man for having a crack at the Gauls.
sentences.zh: 他在公元前 222 年担任执政官，因打击高卢人而成为伟人。

sentences.en: The Romans always liked people who could defeat the Gauls.
sentences.zh: 罗马人总是喜欢那些能击败高卢人的人。

sentences.en: And Calvus's brother, Scipio's father, Publius, people may remember, had been consul in 218, which was the year that Hannibal had invaded Italy.
sentences.zh: 而卡尔武斯的兄弟，也就是西庇阿的父亲普布利乌斯，人们可能还记得，他在公元前 218 年担任执政官，那一年汉尼拔入侵了意大利。

sentences.en: And admittedly, he hadn't exactly covered himself in glory in that campaign.
sentences.zh: 而且不得不承认，他在那场战役中并没有什么光彩的表现。

sentences.en: He tried to stop Hannibal from invading
sentences.zh: 他曾试图阻止汉尼拔入侵

sentences.en: Italy and failed.
sentences.zh: 意大利，但失败了。

sentences.en: And he'd been injured before the Battle of Trebia.
sentences.zh: 而且他在特雷比亚战役前就已经受了伤。

sentences.en: But he hadn't totally screwed things up.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有把事情搞得一团糟。

sentences.en: And compared to the record of other consuls who had taken on Hannibal, I mean, that's, you know, that's not bad.
sentences.zh: 与之前那些对抗过汉尼拔的执政官的记录相比，我的意思是，你知道，那还不算太差。

sentences.en: And it suggested, I think, to the Roman people, to the Roman government, that Publius, he had a kind of a basic competence.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这向罗马人民和罗马政府表明，普布利乌斯具备一种基本的胜任能力。

sentences.en: And that, in the scale of the crisis that Rome was facing, was considered to be enough.
sentences.zh: 在罗马所面临的危机规模下，这被认为是足够了。

sentences.en: And so by 217, both the Scipio brothers, Calvus, who is the young
sentences.zh: 因此到了公元前217年，两位西庇阿兄弟——也就是年轻西庇阿的叔叔卡尔武斯，

sentences.en: Scipio's uncle, and Publius, his father, they have been sent to Iberia, to Spain.
sentences.zh: 以及他的父亲普布利乌斯——他们已经被派往伊比利亚，即西班牙。

sentences.en: And to clarify, so Spain later on, it's obviously an integral part of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 澄清一下，西班牙在后来显然是罗马帝国不可分割的一部分。

sentences.en: Hadrian comes from Spain, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 哈德良皇帝就是来自西班牙，不是吗？

sentences.en: But at the time, so, you know, we're 200 years before the birth of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，你知道，我们是在基督诞生前200年。

sentences.en: Spain is a very alien and exotic and terrifying place for the Romans.
sentences.zh: 对于罗马人来说，西班牙是一个非常陌生、充满异域风情且令人恐惧的地方。

sentences.en: It's like something out of a science fiction epic.
sentences.zh: 就像科幻史诗里的场景一样。

sentences.en: It's like being sent to a hostile planet, because it is teeming with hostile barbarians who clean their teeth with their own urine.
sentences.zh: 就像被派往一颗充满敌意的星球，因为它到处都是用尿液刷牙的敌对蛮族。

sentences.en: I mean, completely shocking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，简直令人震惊。

sentences.en: And they are masters of a lethal weapon.
sentences.zh: 而且他们掌握着一种致命武器。

sentences.en: And this is a short stabbing sword, which works by eviscerating an opponent.
sentences.zh: 这是一种短刺剑，通过剖开对手的身体来发挥作用。

sentences.en: You plunge it in and you slice it up and all the guts spill out.
sentences.zh: 你把它刺进去再搅动，所有的内脏都会流出来。

sentences.en: And the Romans call this weapon a gladius, which is a word that later Roman scholars will derive from the Latin word clades, which means slaughter.
sentences.zh: 罗马人称这种武器为“格拉迪乌斯”（gladius），这个词后来被罗马学者从拉丁语“clades”衍生而来，意为屠杀。

sentences.en: They're kind of synonymous with butchering your enemies.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎成了屠杀敌人的代名词。

sentences.en: And the Romans have already experienced the gladius, because Hannibal has brought lots of
sentences.zh: 罗马人已经领教过格拉迪乌斯了，因为汉尼拔带了许多

sentences.en: Iberians with him to Italy.
sentences.zh: 伊比利亚人来到意大利。

sentences.en: And unsurprisingly, because the Romans are very, very adaptive, particularly when it comes to kind of military matters, they have begun to use the gladius for themselves and
sentences.zh: 不出所料，由于罗马人非常、非常善于适应，特别是在军事事务方面，他们已经开始使用格拉迪乌斯，

sentences.en: are starting to master it.
sentences.zh: 并开始掌握它。

sentences.en: But obviously, it's unsettling to be up against a whole peninsula full of warriors who were born basically to use it.
sentences.zh: 但显然，面对一个满是天生就会使用这种武器的战士的半岛，还是令人不安的。

sentences.en: And so I think that the prime duty of the Scipio brothers when they arrive, and there's a kind of Roman outpost in the northwest of Iberia,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为西庇阿兄弟抵达时的首要任务——他们在伊比利亚西北部有一个罗马前哨站，

sentences.en: basically what's now Catalonia, their prime responsibility is not to be wiped out.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是现在的加泰罗尼亚——他们的首要责任就是不要被全歼。

sentences.en: And this is a huge challenge because they have been sent as the news back in Italy is going from bad to worse.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的挑战，因为他们被派去时，意大利传来的消息正每况愈下。

sentences.en: So Hannibal has been inflicting, you know, these incredible defeats on the Romans that we did in the previous series.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔一直在给罗马人造成我们在上一系列节目中提到的那些令人难以置信的失败。

sentences.en: Lake Trasimene has just been fought, you know, an entire army has been wiped out, a consul killed and all of that.
sentences.zh: 特拉西梅诺湖战役刚刚结束，你知道，整支军队被歼灭，一位执政官阵亡，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And this means that the Senate can't really send, many men or many, you know, or supplies or indeed cash to bribe the local tribes to Spain.
sentences.zh: 这意味着元老院实在无法派遣多少人手、物资，或者现金去贿赂西班牙当地的部落。

sentences.en: And so effectively, the two Scipio brothers are penned into, let's call it Catalonia anachronistically.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，两位西庇阿兄弟被困在了——我们姑且称之为加泰罗尼亚（尽管这是时代错误）——区域内。

sentences.en: It's dangerous for them to venture out of that.
sentences.zh: 冒险离开那里对他们来说很危险。

sentences.en: So if you think of Spain perhaps as being a little bit like Arrakis, Dune in the Frank Herbert novels, you know, they are hemmed in and they feel that it is perilous to leave that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你把西班牙想象成有点像弗兰克·赫伯特小说《沙丘》里的厄拉科斯，你知道，他们被围困在那里，觉得离开那里非常危险。

sentences.en: And I think that if people have a sense of this whole story that we're doing today as something that could very easily provide the plot of a kind of one of those epic
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果人们觉得我们今天讲的这个故事，很容易就能成为那种设定在遥远星球上的史诗级

sentences.en: science fiction novels set on distant planets, they will not be far wrong.
sentences.zh: 科幻小说的情节，那他们一点也没错。

sentences.en: The clash of mighty galactic empires, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 强大银河帝国之间的冲突，就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So to remind people exactly where we are, we are back at the point when Hannibal is kind of cutting a swathe through Italy.
sentences.zh: 为了提醒大家我们现在的进度，我们回到了汉尼拔在意大利横冲直撞的时期。

sentences.en: We're with the two
sentences.zh: 我们现在和两位

sentences.en: Scipio brothers who are our Scipio, so the long-haired boke.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿兄弟在一起，也就是我们的西庇阿——那个长发家伙的

sentences.en: It's his father and uncle.
sentences.zh: 父亲和叔叔。

sentences.en: And so we've sort of gone back in time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们算是回到了过去。

sentences.en: So we're in Spain.
sentences.zh: 我们在西班牙。

sentences.en: And the problem for them is that they are now facing not just, you know, one Carthaginian general and not just the Iberians with these fancy swords,
sentences.zh: 他们面临的问题是，现在面对的不仅仅是一位迦太基将军和那些拿着精美宝剑的伊比利亚人，

sentences.en: but the entire Carthaginian Empire now controls the whole of the southern part of the Iberian peninsula, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 而是整个迦太基帝国现在控制了伊比利亚半岛的整个南部，不是吗？

sentences.en: And the guy in charge of the Carthaginians at this point in this part of the world is Hannibal's younger brother, Hasdrubal.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，在这个地区负责迦太基事务的人是汉尼拔的弟弟哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: And he has with him a pretty mighty force, 13,000 infantrymen, 3,000 cavalry.
sentences.zh: 他拥有一支相当强大的军队，13000名步兵，3000名骑兵。

sentences.en: He has 21 war elephants.
sentences.zh: 他有21头战象。

sentences.en: He's got all these mines that are the key really to Spain's wealth.
sentences.zh: 他拥有所有那些矿山，那才是西班牙财富的关键所在。

sentences.en: It's what makes Spain so attractive to outsiders.
sentences.zh: 这正是西班牙对外来者如此有吸引力的原因。

sentences.en: So gold, silver, copper.
sentences.zh: 黄金、白银、铜。

sentences.en: And he has a city that we talked about last time.
sentences.zh: 他还有一座我们上次谈到的城市。

sentences.en: They've called it Carthage.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为迦太基。

sentences.en: The Romans call it
sentences.zh: 罗马人称之为

sentences.en: this is the sort of center, the base of the Carthaginian Empire in Spain.
sentences.zh: 这是迦太基帝国在西班牙的中心和基地。

sentences.en: And this city is on four hills overlooking a fantastic harbor.
sentences.zh: 这座城市坐落在四座小山上，俯瞰着一个绝佳的港口。

sentences.en: It's to this day one of Spain's, Cartagena is one of
sentences.zh: 直到今天，卡塔赫纳仍然是西班牙的

sentences.en: Spain's key naval bases.
sentences.zh: 关键海军基地之一。

sentences.en: You know, like so many cities across the Mediterranean world, it's got these amazing fortifications.
sentences.zh: 你知道，像地中海世界的许多城市一样，它拥有令人惊叹的防御工事。

sentences.en: And it has a direct road link with the mines that makes it extremely rich.
sentences.zh: 它有一条直通矿山的道路，这使它极其富有。

sentences.en: And basically, if Hasdrubal, the Carthaginian, can keep hold of this, then the Scipio brothers,
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果迦太基人哈斯德鲁巴能守住这里，那么西庇阿兄弟，

sentences.en: basically they can do what they like, but they're not going to dislodge him from the Iberian Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 他们想做什么都行，但无法将他从伊比利亚半岛赶走。

sentences.en: So the Greek historian Polybius, who is our best source for the Punic Wars, I mean, he describes it as the chief ornament and the center of the Carthaginian Empire in Spain.
sentences.zh: 希腊历史学家波利比乌斯是我们了解布匿战争的最佳来源，他将其描述为迦太基帝国在西班牙的“主要装饰和中心”。

sentences.en: Because not only is it linked to the mines in the hinterland, but it is also, of course, open to the sea.
sentences.zh: 因为它不仅与内陆的矿山相连，当然也面向大海。

sentences.en: So it's what enables New Carthage to communicate with Carthage, and of course, with Italy.
sentences.zh: 所以它使新迦太基能够与迦太基，当然还有意大利进行联络。

sentences.en: And what this means is that Hasdrubal and the powers in Carthage can coordinate to try and raise reinforcements that can then be sent onwards to Italy.
sentences.zh: 这意味着哈斯德鲁巴和迦太基的当权者可以协调，试图筹集增援部队，然后送往意大利。

sentences.en: And this is absolutely, goes without saying, the last thing that the Romans want, they do not want a second Barker brother.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是不用说的，罗马人最不希望看到的事情，他们不想要第二个巴卡兄弟。

sentences.en: So Hannibal Barker, Hasdrubal Barker, they do not want Hasdrubal Barker turning up in Italy with yet another massive Carthaginian army,
sentences.zh: 所以汉尼拔·巴卡、哈斯德鲁巴·巴卡，他们不希望哈斯德鲁巴·巴卡带着另一支庞大的迦太基军队出现在意大利，

sentences.en: with his elephants and his Numidians and his Spaniards with their terrifying stabbing swords, and so on.
sentences.zh: 带着他的大象、努米底亚人和拿着恐怖刺剑的西班牙人等等。

sentences.en: So essentially, the Scipio brothers are where they are in the northwest corner of Iberia,
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，西庇阿兄弟之所以待在伊比利亚的西北角，

sentences.en: by the Pyrenees, essentially to block off Hasdrubal's access route to southern Gaul so that he can't follow Hannibal into Italy.
sentences.zh: 就在比利牛斯山脉旁边，基本上就是为了切断哈斯德鲁巴通往南高卢的通道，这样他就无法跟随汉尼拔进入意大利。

sentences.en: And their objective is not just to stop Hannibal, but to try and conquer and win over as many of the Iberian tribes as possible, and ideally, you know, conquer them for Rome.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标不仅是阻止汉尼拔，还要尽可能征服并争取更多的伊比利亚部落，理想情况下，为罗马征服他们。

sentences.en: But if they can't do that, then at the very least, kind of foster anti-Carthaginian
sentences.zh: 但如果做不到这一点，至少要培养反迦太基的

sentences.en: feeling, so that Hasdrubal will have his hands full trying to kind of put out rebellions in Spain.
sentences.zh: 情绪，这样哈斯德鲁巴就会忙于在西班牙平定叛乱。

sentences.en: And Hasdrubal's goal is obviously to raise an enormous army and march through Gaul into Italy.
sentences.zh: 而哈斯德鲁巴的目标显然是筹集一支庞大的军队，穿过高卢进入意大利。

sentences.en: And for the Romans, the supreme moment of peril comes in the spring of 215, which is the year after
sentences.zh: 对于罗马人来说，最危险的时刻出现在公元前215年的春天，也就是

sentences.en: Cannae.
sentences.zh: 坎尼战役之后的一年。

sentences.en: And Hasdrubal has raised an enormous task force.
sentences.zh: 哈斯德鲁巴已经组建了一支庞大的特遣部队。

sentences.en: And he leaves New Carthage.
sentences.zh: 他离开了新迦太基。

sentences.en: And as Hannibal had done three years before, he advances northwards at the head of this vast force.
sentences.zh: 正如汉尼拔三年前所做的那样，他率领这支庞大的军队向北推进。

sentences.en: And his aim is to cross the Pyrenees, advance through Gaul, and join his brother in Italy.
sentences.zh: 他的目标是翻越比利牛斯山脉，穿过高卢，与他在意大利的兄弟会合。

sentences.en: And if he's successful, then Hannibal's forces will be doubled.
sentences.zh: 如果他成功了，汉尼拔的兵力将增加一倍。

sentences.en: And it is hard to see in the wake of Cannae how the Romans then would have been able to carry on the fight.
sentences.zh: 很难想象在坎尼战役之后，罗马人还能如何继续战斗。

sentences.en: So this is really a crucial moment in the war.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是战争中至关重要的时刻。

sentences.en: So the two Scipios, they are basically standing in his way.
sentences.zh: 所以两位西庇阿兄弟基本上挡在了他的路上。

sentences.en: And they meet Hasdrubal just south of the river Ebro, outside a town called Ibera.
sentences.zh: 他们在埃布罗河南岸，伊贝拉镇外遇到了哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: And this is actually one of the most significant battles in history, arguably, that nobody has ever heard of.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是历史上最重大的战役之一，可以说，却鲜为人知。

sentences.en: Because as you say, if Hasdrubal manages to cross the Alps, join Hannibal in Italy, that looks really dicey for the Romans.
