sentences.zh: 因为任命指挥官的通常不是元老院吗，而不是罗马人民？

sentences.en: Because isn't normally the Senate that appoints commanders rather than the Roman people?
sentences.zh: 是的，这非常不寻常。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very unusual.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，元老院非常看重自己的特权。

sentences.en: Because as you say, the Senate is very jealous of its prerogative.
sentences.zh: 元老院有权任命指挥官。

sentences.en: The Senate has the right to appoint commanders.
sentences.zh: 人民为什么要插手这种重要的事情呢？

sentences.en: What are the people doing poking their noses into, you know, this important business?
sentences.zh: 因为人们理所当然地认为指挥官应该是民选的行政长官。

sentences.en: Because it is taken for granted that commanders should be elected magistrates.
sentences.zh: 但西庇阿不是民选的行政长官。

sentences.en: But Scipio is not an elected magistrate.
sentences.zh: 他是一个平民，一个私人公民。

sentences.en: He is a privatus, a private citizen.
sentences.zh: 而且罗马的习俗也倾向于重视经验。

sentences.en: And it is also the Roman custom to put a premium on experience.
sentences.zh: 他们倾向于认为年轻不是一种意气风发，而是一种潜在的危险。

sentences.en: They tend to regard youth not as something dashing, but as something potentially sinister.
sentences.zh: 通常认为40岁以下的罗马指挥官是冲动、固执和鲁莽的。

sentences.en: That a Roman commander who is under the age of 40 is generally assumed to be kind of impulsive and headstrong and rash.
sentences.zh: 所以听众们可能想知道，这个25岁的西庇阿，这个私人公民，到底是怎么得到这个指挥权的？

sentences.en: So listeners may therefore be wondering, well, how on earth did the 25 year old Scipio, you know, this private citizen, how on earth did he manage to get this command?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，毫无疑问，人民崇拜他。

sentences.en: I mean, it's undoubtedly the case that the people adore him.
sentences.zh: 他很有魅力，意气风发，在与汉尼拔的战争那种单调乏味的磨难中，他为他们增添了一抹亮色。

sentences.en: He's glamorous, he's dashing, he provides them with, you know, a touch of colour amid the kind of monochrome grind of the war against
sentences.zh: 虽然与此同时，元老院里很多人确实对他心存疑虑，

sentences.en: Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 但我认为也有很多人能认识到专门派他去西班牙的好处。

sentences.en: And although at the same time, although lots of people in the Senate are indeed suspicious
sentences.zh: 因为记住，他是曾在西班牙任职的指挥官之一的儿子。

sentences.en: of him, I think there are also lots of them that can recognise the advantages of sending him specifically to Spain.
sentences.zh: 他还是另一位指挥官的侄子。

sentences.en: Because remember, he is the son of one of the commanders who'd been in Spain.
sentences.zh: 所以西庇阿这个名字在伊比利亚有着真正的声望。

sentences.en: And he is the nephew of another of those commanders.
sentences.zh: 我认为即使在元老院里，也有人觉得，如果不利用这一点，那我们就是疯了。

sentences.en: So the name of Scipio in Iberia has a real cachet.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，问题在于他们不想被视为任命了一个25岁的年轻人。

sentences.en: And I think that even in the Senate, there are people who feel, well, we would be mad not to capitalise on this.
sentences.zh: 如果他们这样做，就会开创一个危险的先例。

sentences.en: The issue for them is, they don't want to be seen to be appointing a 25 year old.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是公众投票发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: That if they do it, it would establish a sinister precedent.
sentences.zh: 他们可以让人民投票选他。

sentences.en: And so that's where the popular vote comes in.
sentences.zh: 本质上，他们是在推卸责任。

sentences.en: They can get the people to vote for him.
sentences.zh: 所以西庇阿得到了他的指挥权。

sentences.en: And essentially, they're kind of washing hands of the responsibility.
sentences.zh: 他离开罗马，抵达西班牙。

sentences.en: So Scipio, he gets his command.
sentences.zh: 他所面临的局势非常非常严峻。

sentences.en: He leaves Rome, he arrives in Spain.
sentences.zh: 显然，罗马人已经输掉了两场重大战役。

sentences.en: And the situation that he finds waiting for him is a very, very rocky one.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在西班牙西北部飞地的兵力严重损耗。

sentences.en: So obviously, the Romans have lost two major battles.
sentences.zh: 伊比利亚部落，你知道的，他们正忙着用尿液刷牙。

sentences.en: So their numbers in their kind of enclave in the northwest of Spain are badly depleted.
sentences.zh: 他们正在磨快他们的刺剑，诸如此类。

sentences.en: The Iberian tribes, you know, they're busy cleaning their teeth with urine.
sentences.zh: 这些人只尊重成功。

sentences.en: They're sharpening their stabbing swords, all of that.
sentences.zh: 这意味着既然罗马人已经被迦太基人彻底击败，他们更有可能倒向迦太基一边。

sentences.en: These are people who only really respect success.
sentences.zh: 这对迦太基指挥官来说显然是极好的，因为他们的兵力现在大增，能够派出三支军队上战场。

sentences.en: And this in turn means that now the Romans have been so comprehensively defeated by the
sentences.zh: 所以，一支由汉尼拔的弟弟哈斯德鲁巴率领，驻扎在西班牙中部，靠近今天的托莱多市。

sentences.en: Carthaginians, they are much likelier to swing Carthaginian-wise.
sentences.zh: 另一支由汉尼拔最小的弟弟马戈率领，靠近赫拉克勒斯之柱，也就是今天的直布罗陀。

sentences.en: And this obviously is brilliant for the Carthaginian commanders, because their numbers have now swollen, and they are able to put three armies in the field.
sentences.zh: 第三支军队在塔古斯河口。

sentences.en: So there is one under Hasdrubal, Hannibal's younger brother, which is stationed in central Spain, near what would today be the city of Toledo.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，那就是你最喜欢的城市，

sentences.en: There's another under Mago, who is Hannibal's youngest brother, near the pillars of Hercules, what today is Gibraltar.
sentences.zh: 里斯本。

sentences.en: And there is a third army by the mouth of the Tagus.
sentences.zh: 我爱里斯本。

sentences.en: So that is, Dominic, your favourite city,
sentences.zh: 所以迦太基人并没有考虑，他们不认为自己需要进行防御战来维持在西班牙的立足点。

sentences.en: Lisbon.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是在考虑扩张他们的帝国。

sentences.en: I love Lisbon.
sentences.zh: 他们想征服西班牙北部。

sentences.en: So the Carthaginians are not thinking about, they don't think they're going to be having to fight a defensive war to maintain their foothold in Spain.
sentences.zh: 他们想获得更多的人力。

sentences.en: They actually are thinking about expanding their empire, as it were.
sentences.zh: 他们想获得更多的矿产和自然资源。

sentences.en: They want to conquer northern Spain.
sentences.zh: 一旦做到这一点，他们认为，好吧，我们就搞定了伊比利亚半岛。

sentences.en: They want to get more manpower.
sentences.zh: 然后哈斯德鲁巴就可以带领一支特遣部队穿过法国南部，翻越阿尔卑斯山，进入意大利，正如我们长期以来所希望的那样。

sentences.en: They want to get more mines, more natural resources.
sentences.zh: 那一如既往是他们的首要目标。

sentences.en: And once they've done that, they think, right, we'll finish with the Iberian Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then Hasdrubal can lead a task force into, you know, through southern France, across the Alps, into Italy, as we have been hoping to do for so long.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That, as always, is their prime goal.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，那个冬天，迦太基人并没有撤退到他们在新迦太基的基地，而是留在了前线基地，因为他们处于进攻态势。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，是他们在主导这场战争。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So actually, that winter, the Carthaginians do not retire to their base at New Carthage, but they remain in their forward bases because they are on the front foot.
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，他们蔑视西庇阿。

sentences.en: It's they, they believe, who are prosecuting the war.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没把他考虑在内。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得罗马人已经被打败了。

sentences.en: And it's clear as well that they regard Scipio with contempt.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们现在的重点基本上是征服剩余的伊比利亚部落。

sentences.en: They haven't factored him into this at all.
sentences.zh: 但这将被证明是一个非常非常严重的错误，因为年轻的西庇阿带着一个非常非常大胆的计划抵达了战场。

sentences.en: They feel that the Romans have been beaten.
sentences.zh: 所以那个春天，他带上了他仅有的士兵。

sentences.en: And this is, you know, and their focus now is essentially, as you say, on conquering the remaining Iberian tribes.
sentences.zh: 大约有2万名步兵和2500名骑兵，他沿着海岸向南进发，就像他父亲和叔叔前一年所做的那样。

sentences.en: But this is going to prove a very, very serious mistake because the young Scipio has arrived to take up his command with a very, very bold plan in his head indeed.
sentences.zh: 在他行进时，罗马舰队在侧翼掩护。

sentences.en: And so that spring, his first, you know, it's his last soldier that he has.
sentences.zh: 这支舰队由他最亲密的朋友盖乌斯·利利乌斯指挥。

sentences.en: And it comes to about 20,000 infantry, 2,500 cavalry, and he heads south along the coast, as his father and uncle had done the previous year.
sentences.zh: 利利乌斯是特遣部队中唯一知道他们要去哪里的人。

sentences.en: And as he goes, he is shadowed by the Roman fleet.
sentences.zh: 唯一一个西庇阿信任并告知他那个绝妙计划的人。

sentences.en: And this is commanded by his closest friend, a guy called Gaius Lilius.
sentences.zh: 于是他们沿着道路向南行军，不停地走啊走。

sentences.en: And Lilius is the only other person in the task force who knows where they are heading.
sentences.zh: 终于，在他们出发一周后，也就是第七天，他们抵达了目的地。

sentences.en: The only person that
sentences.zh: 而这个目的地，多米尼克，就是伟大的新迦太基城。

sentences.en: Scipio has entrusted with his brilliant plan.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个极其大胆的战略。

sentences.en: So southwards they march along the road, on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 于是他们沿着道路一路向南，不停地走啊走。

sentences.en: And finally, a week after they've left, so on the seventh day, they arrive before their destination.
sentences.zh: 终于，在他们出发一周后，也就是第七天，他们抵达了目的地前方。

sentences.en: And this destination, Dominic, is the great city of New Carthage.
sentences.zh: 而这个目的地，多米尼克，就是伟大的新迦太基城。

sentences.en: It's obviously an incredibly bold strategy.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个极其大胆的策略。

sentences.en: It's been fostered by the fact that Scipio knows that the Carthaginian armies are at least 10 days march away.
sentences.zh: 这得益于西庇阿知道迦太基军队至少还有10天的路程。

sentences.en: And that the garrison that has been left in New Carthage, it's basically only about a thousand strong.
sentences.zh: 而且留在新迦太基的守军，基本上只有一千人左右。

sentences.en: But even so, we said how, you know, it has these kind of bristling fortifications.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，我们之前说过，它有着那种令人望而生畏的防御工事。

sentences.en: It's a very, very strong city.
sentences.zh: 那是一座非常、非常坚固的城市。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a big, big ask to take it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，攻下它是一个非常、非常艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: And I think that Scipio's men, when they realise the job that their young general has set them, you know, they feel a bit alarmed.
sentences.zh: 我想西庇阿的士兵们在意识到他们年轻的统帅给他们指派的任务时，心里多少有些惊慌。

sentences.en: They think, oh God, actually, you know, everybody says about young commanders, it's true.
sentences.zh: 他们心想，天哪，说实话，每个人对年轻指挥官的评价确实没错。

sentences.en: They are rash.
sentences.zh: 他们鲁莽。

sentences.en: They are headstrong.
sentences.zh: 他们固执。

sentences.en: They do come up with mad ideas.
sentences.zh: 他们确实会想出疯狂的主意。

sentences.en: But Scipio summons his men and he addresses them and he appears sublimely self-confident.
sentences.zh: 但西庇阿召集了他的士兵，向他们发表讲话，表现得极其自信。

sentences.en: And he tells them, it is the god Neptune who first suggested this plan to me.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他们，是海神尼普顿首先向他提出了这个计划。

sentences.en: So he's now moved on from talking to Jupiter.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在已经不再谈论朱庇特了。

sentences.en: He's talking to Neptune, the god of the sea.
sentences.zh: 他现在谈论的是海神尼普顿。

sentences.en: He appeared to me in a dream
sentences.zh: 他在梦中向我显现，

sentences.en: and has promised to show his support for us by means of a spectacular sign.
sentences.zh: 并承诺会通过一个壮观的迹象来展示对我们的支持。

sentences.en: Well, to be fair, this is very, you'd compare with Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 嗯，平心而论，这确实可以和亚历山大大帝相提并论。

sentences.en: This is certainly the kind of stuff that Alexander the Great would come out with.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是亚历山大大帝会说的那种话。

sentences.en: And people would say, hurrah, yeah, I completely believe this.
sentences.zh: 人们会欢呼，是的，我完全相信这一点。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 我们干吧。

sentences.en: And actually, you know, it's a good comparison.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这确实是一个很好的类比。

sentences.en: What happens immediately is that Lilius, the naval commander, you know, he assembles his ships and they surround the harbour, blocking off access.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情是，海军指挥官利利乌斯集结了他的船只，包围了港口，切断了通道。

sentences.en: And the main body of Scipio's men launch a massive frontal assault on the city walls.
sentences.zh: 而西庇阿的主力部队对城墙发动了大规模的正面进攻。

sentences.en: And the defenders are entirely focused on resisting this.
sentences.zh: 守军的注意力完全集中在抵御这次进攻上。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Scipio has recruited a crack squad of elite handpicked men and he takes them on a secret mission because north of the city, there stretches a lagoon.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，西庇阿挑选了一支精锐突击队，带着他们执行秘密任务，因为在城市北面，有一片泻湖。

sentences.en: And because the waters are normally so deep and because every defender in New Carthage is required to stave off this kind of main Roman
sentences.zh: 由于那里的水通常很深，而且新迦太基的每一名守军都被要求去抵御罗马人的这种正面

sentences.en: assault, the walls that rise above the lagoon are unguarded because they assume that, well, no one will be able to cross the lagoon.
sentences.zh: 进攻，所以泻湖上方的城墙无人防守，因为他们认为，没人能穿过那片泻湖。

sentences.en: So Scipio arrives with his crack squad of elite handpicked men on the shores of the lagoon.
sentences.zh: 于是，西庇阿带着他的精锐突击队来到了泻湖岸边。

sentences.en: And they look out and there it is.
sentences.zh: 他们望向前方，目标就在那里。

sentences.en: And then beyond the lagoon are the northern walls of New Carthage.
sentences.zh: 泻湖对面就是新迦太基的北城墙。

sentences.en: And as they gaze at the walls, there is a palpable miracle because a heron lands and stands in the water.
sentences.zh: 当他们凝视城墙时，一个显而易见的奇迹发生了，一只苍鹭降落在水中。

sentences.en: And this reveals to the Romans that the waters are ebbing.
sentences.zh: 这向罗马人揭示了水位正在下降。

sentences.en: You say a miracle, but isn't that pretty standard with waters that they ebb and flow?
sentences.zh: 你说这是奇迹，但水位涨落不是常态吗？

sentences.en: It turns out that this is, in fact, a regular phenomenon, that it happens every so often.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这确实是一种规律现象，每隔一段时间就会发生。

sentences.en: It does not happen every day.
sentences.zh: 它不是每天都发生。

sentences.en: It's not a regular tide, but every so often the tide does go out.
sentences.zh: 这不是常规的潮汐，但每隔一段时间潮水确实会退去。

sentences.en: And Scipio has been informed about this and he's worked out that this is the moment when he needs to be there.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿对此早有了解，他计算出这就是他需要到达那里的时刻。

sentences.en: But obviously, he doesn't tell this to his men.
sentences.zh: 但显然，他没有告诉他的士兵。

sentences.en: And they all assume that this is the sign from Neptune that
sentences.zh: 他们都以为这是尼普顿给出的迹象，

sentences.en: Scipio had promised them.
sentences.zh: 正如西庇阿向他们承诺的那样。

sentences.en: And so they wade in through the shallows, reach the base of the walls.
sentences.zh: 于是他们涉水穿过浅滩，到达了城墙底部。

sentences.en: They've brought ladders with them.
sentences.zh: 他们随身带着梯子。

sentences.en: They put them up against the walls.
sentences.zh: 他们把梯子架在城墙上。

sentences.en: They climb over and there is no one to stop them.
sentences.zh: 他们爬了上去，没有人能阻止他们。

sentences.en: And now they can rush forward.
sentences.zh: 现在他们可以冲进去了。

sentences.en: They can open the gates of the city.
sentences.zh: 他们可以打开城门。

sentences.en: The Romans who've been doing the full frontal assault can pile in as well.
sentences.zh: 正在进行正面强攻的罗马人也可以一拥而入。

sentences.en: And there is unbelievable slaughter.
sentences.zh: 接着就是难以置信的屠杀。

sentences.en: And we know this because Polybius, this Greek historian, he goes on to interview Lilius, who is Scipio's friend who'd been in command of the fleet.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为希腊历史学家波利比乌斯后来采访了西庇阿的朋友、舰队指挥官利利乌斯。

sentences.en: And he revealed just how brutal the slaughter had been.
sentences.zh: 他揭示了当时的屠杀是多么残酷。

sentences.en: So to quote Polybius, the practice of the Romans is to inspire terror.
sentences.zh: 引用波利比乌斯的话，罗马人的做法是制造恐怖。

sentences.en: And so when they capture a city, you will often see not just the corpses of human beings, but dogs cut in half and the dismembered limbs of other animals.
sentences.zh: 所以当你攻下一座城市时，你经常看到的不仅是人类的尸体，还有被砍成两半的狗和其他动物的残肢。

sentences.en: And Lilius specifies to Polybius that this is what was happening in New Carthage after the Romans had got in.
sentences.zh: 利利乌斯向波利比乌斯详细说明了罗马人进入新迦太基后发生的情况。

sentences.en: And so unsurprisingly, the Carthaginian commander, seeing the horror, realising that he has no prospect of keeping the city, he duly surrenders.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，迦太基指挥官目睹了惨状，意识到自己已无望守住这座城市，便顺从地投降了。

sentences.en: And so the slaughter stops.
sentences.zh: 屠杀随之停止。

sentences.en: And New Carthage, unbelievably, is Scipios.
sentences.zh: 新迦太基，令人难以置信地，归西庇阿所有了。

sentences.en: He has seized the great nerve centre of the Carthaginian Empire.
sentences.zh: 他夺取了迦太基帝国的核心枢纽。

sentences.en: I mean, an amazing coup.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一次惊人的政变。

sentences.en: So this is an extraordinary moment, because what this has done is it means that the Romans now have the wealth of New Carthage, they have the supplies, they have the resources,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非凡的时刻，因为这意味着罗马人现在拥有了新迦太基的财富、补给和资源，

sentences.en: they have the harbour.
sentences.zh: 他们还拥有了港口。

sentences.en: So they have a wonderful link now with the sea.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在拥有了一个通往大海的绝佳连接点。

sentences.en: And Scipio immediately turns it into what Polybius calls a workshop of war, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 西庇阿立刻把它变成了波利比乌斯所说的“战争工坊”，不是吗？

sentences.en: So he starts to recruit troops, he's drilling them, he's kind of endlessly schooling them in kind of the tactics they will need that he has learned from Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 他开始招募军队，进行操练，不断地用他从汉尼拔那里学到的战术来训练他们。

sentences.en: He's making weapons.
sentences.zh: 他在制造武器。

sentences.en: And the PR, the propaganda effects of this, perhaps the most crucial element, because basically, this is sending a message to the people of the Iberian Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 而公关和宣传效果，也许是最关键的因素，因为这基本上是在向伊比利亚半岛的人民传递一个信息。

sentences.en: The Romans are back, and they're here in a big way, and they are the winners now.
sentences.zh: 罗马人回来了，他们以强大的姿态回归，他们现在是赢家。

sentences.en: Yeah, and the Iberians love a winner.
sentences.zh: 是的，伊比利亚人喜欢赢家。

sentences.en: So by the spring of 208, Hasdrubal knows he's got a massive crisis on his hands, because he's lost his capital, but he is now increasingly losing the loyalty of all
sentences.zh: 所以到了公元前208年春天，哈斯德鲁巴知道他面临着巨大的危机，因为他失去了首都，而且他正逐渐失去所有

sentences.en: these kind of various Iberian warlords, who are thinking, well, Scipio's a winner, let's back him.
sentences.zh: 那些伊比利亚军阀的忠诚，他们心想，西庇阿是个赢家，我们支持他吧。

sentences.en: And a whole posse of warlords by the spring of 208 have decided that they are actively going to back the Romans.
sentences.zh: 到208年春天，一大批军阀已经决定积极支持罗马人。

sentences.en: And so again, to quote Polybius, they all prostrated themselves before Scipio and hailed him as king.
sentences.zh: 再次引用波利比乌斯的话，他们都匍匐在西庇阿面前，尊他为王。

sentences.en: And of course, the word king is a very dirty word to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 当然，“王”这个词对罗马人来说是一个非常肮脏的词。

sentences.en: They are republic, they don't like kings.
sentences.zh: 他们是共和国，他们不喜欢国王。

sentences.en: But Scipio accepts that, you know, the name has a kind of glamour that will help his cause.
sentences.zh: 但西庇阿接受了，因为他知道，这个头衔有一种能帮助他事业的魅力。

sentences.en: And so he, you know, he accepts it, which in the long run won't go down well in Rome, but you know, needs muSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他接受了，从长远来看，这在罗马不会受到欢迎，但你知道，形势所迫。

sentences.en: So the issue now for Hasdrubal, his rival, Hasdrubal knows that basically the entire war hinges on this, right?
sentences.zh: 现在哈斯德鲁巴面临的问题是，他的对手知道整场战争基本上都取决于这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: Because Carthage really, really needs Spain to continue being at, as it were, the top table of international kind of superpower rivalry.
sentences.zh: 因为迦太基确实非常需要西班牙，才能继续保持在国际超级大国竞争的顶尖行列。

sentences.en: Well, and more than that, if they lose Spain, then there's no way that Hannibal can win in Italy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不仅如此，如果他们失去了西班牙，那么汉尼拔就不可能在意大利获胜。

sentences.en: Because if supplies and troops from Spain cannot reach Italy, then in the long run, Hannibal will lose.
sentences.zh: 因为如果来自西班牙的补给和军队无法到达意大利，那么从长远来看，汉尼拔必败无疑。

sentences.en: So do you think Hasdrubal at this point is thinking, right, well, I need to really force the issue.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为哈斯德鲁巴此时在想，好吧，我真的需要孤注一掷了。

sentences.en: Let's get this over and done with now, because having lost New Carthage, I can't hang around.
sentences.zh: 现在就了结这件事吧，因为失去了新迦太基，我不能再拖延了。

sentences.en: So this is why he basically rolls the dice and says, right, we'll go for Italy right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他基本上孤注一掷，说，好吧，我们现在就去意大利。

sentences.en: We will march there with the expeditionary force to give my brother the reinforcements he needs, and let's finish this.
sentences.zh: 我们将带着远征军进军那里，给我哥哥他所需的增援，让我们结束这一切。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so it is obvious to both sides that this is the great fulcrum point of the whole war.
sentences.zh: 所以双方都很清楚，这是整场战争的关键转折点。

sentences.en: This is the moment of supreme crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是至关重要的危机时刻。

sentences.en: Everything hangs on what happens next.
sentences.zh: 一切都取决于接下来发生的事情。

sentences.en: So obviously, the Romans are desperate to stop Hasdrubal.
sentences.zh: 显然，罗马人拼命想要阻止哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: The best way for them to stop Hasdrubal joining up with Hannibal is to prevent him leaving Iberia at all.
sentences.zh: 阻止哈斯德鲁巴与汉尼拔会合的最好方法，就是阻止他离开伊比利亚。

sentences.en: So early that summer, Scipio advances into the depths of
sentences.zh: 所以那年夏天初，西庇阿深入

sentences.en: Iberia.
sentences.zh: 伊比利亚腹地。

sentences.en: He attacks Hasdrubal's base, and he manages to inflict serious casualties.
sentences.zh: 他袭击了哈斯德鲁巴的基地，并成功造成了严重伤亡。

sentences.en: But he can't prevent Hasdrubal from doing a withdrawal from his base.
sentences.zh: 但他无法阻止哈斯德鲁巴从基地撤离。

sentences.en: And nor, over the next few months, can he prevent Hasdrubal from rebuilding his army.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几个月里，他也无法阻止哈斯德鲁巴重建军队。

sentences.en: And by the winter of 2008, Hasdrubal has advanced through
sentences.zh: 到了公元前208年冬天，哈斯德鲁巴已经穿过

sentences.en: Spain, over the Pyrenees, and has arrived in southern Gaul, where he is wintering.
sentences.zh: 西班牙，翻越比利牛斯山脉，抵达了高卢南部，并在那里过冬。

sentences.en: And wintering in southern Gaul gives him the opportunity to recruit lots of warriors from Gaul.
sentences.zh: 在高卢南部过冬让他有机会招募大量高卢战士。

sentences.en: The Gauls hate the
sentences.zh: 高卢人痛恨

sentences.en: Romans.
sentences.zh: 罗马人。

sentences.en: This is what Hannibal had done when he'd gone.
sentences.zh: 这就是汉尼拔当年所做的事情。

sentences.en: So his army is now really substantial.
sentences.zh: 所以他的军队现在非常庞大。

sentences.en: And come spring the next year, so the campaigning season, he leads his army, complete with 10 elephants, over the Alps.
sentences.zh: 第二年春天，也就是作战季节到来时，他率领军队，带着10头大象，翻越了阿尔卑斯山。

sentences.en: And people may be wondering, well, we hear all about Hannibal crossing the Alps.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会想，我们听说过汉尼拔翻越阿尔卑斯山的事。

sentences.en: We never hear about Hasdrubal crossing the Alps, what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我们从未听说过哈斯德鲁巴翻越阿尔卑斯山，这到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: I mean, the reason is that he does it expertly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，原因是他做得非常专业。

sentences.en: He does it with incredible competence.
sentences.zh: 他做得非常出色。

sentences.en: And I think essentially the reason that we remember
sentences.zh: 我认为我们之所以记住

sentences.en: Hannibal's crossing is that he doesn't do it nearly as competently as Hasdrubal did.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔的翻越，是因为他做得远不如哈斯德鲁巴那么专业。

sentences.en: Anyway, so Hasdrubal descends from the Alps, he arrives in northern Italy, and the Romans' worst nightmare has happened.
sentences.zh: 总之，哈斯德鲁巴从阿尔卑斯山下来，抵达了意大利北部，罗马人最可怕的噩梦成真了。

sentences.en: There are now two huge armies, each one led by a Barker brother in their backyard.
sentences.zh: 现在有两支庞大的军队，每一支都由一名巴卡家族的兄弟率领，就在他们的后院。

sentences.en: There are two consuls in Rome who have the job of stopping these two brothers.
sentences.zh: 罗马有两位执政官，他们的任务是阻止这两兄弟。

sentences.en: And one is in the north.
sentences.zh: 一个在北方。

sentences.en: He has six legions and he's got to stop Hasdrubal.
sentences.zh: 他有六个军团，必须阻止哈斯德鲁巴。

sentences.en: And then there's one in the south with seven legions who's meant to be bottling up Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 另一个在南方，带着七个军团，负责困住汉尼拔。

sentences.en: So the guy in charge of the northern legions, I read in your notes, Tom, he is called Marcus Livius Salenitor.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我在你的笔记里读到，负责北方军团的那个人叫马库斯·利维乌斯·萨利纳托尔。
zh_words: 马库斯·利维乌斯·萨利纳托尔

sentences.en: And he is, and I quote from your notes, a gloomy eccentric with terrible personal hygiene.
sentences.zh: 而且，引用你的笔记，他是一个“个人卫生极差的阴郁怪人”。

sentences.en: I assume that all eccentrics have bad personal hygiene.
sentences.zh: 我假设所有的怪人个人卫生都不好。

sentences.en: How does his poor personal hygiene manifest itself, would you say?
sentences.zh: 你会说他糟糕的个人卫生是如何表现出来的呢？

sentences.en: He's feeling very hard done by.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己受到了很不公正的对待。

sentences.en: And so as a protest, he has refused to wash or cut his hair.
sentences.zh: 因此作为抗议，他拒绝洗澡或剪头发。

sentences.en: And so he's notorious for his body odour.
sentences.zh: 所以他以体味难闻而臭名昭著。

sentences.en: That's no way to inspire your men.
sentences.zh: 那可不是激励士兵的好方法。

sentences.en: And what about the guy in the south?
sentences.zh: 那南方的那个人呢？

sentences.en: So the guy in the south is a member of the Claudian dynasty, one of the oldest and most prestigious dynasties.
sentences.zh: 南方的那个人是克劳狄王朝的成员，这是最古老、最显赫的王朝之一。

sentences.en: So he's called Gaius Claudius Nero and he is beautifully groomed, is he?
sentences.zh: 所以他叫盖乌斯·克劳狄乌斯·尼禄，他仪表堂堂，是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, not a hint of body odour.
sentences.zh: 是的，一点体味都没有。

sentences.en: These two blokes, perhaps because of their dispute about grooming, despise each other.
sentences.zh: 这两个家伙，也许是因为在仪表上的分歧，互相鄙视。

sentences.en: They absolutely loathe each other.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对厌恶对方。

sentences.en: And so this is obviously a potential worry.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个潜在的隐患。

sentences.en: I mean, will they be able to team up?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们能合作吗？

sentences.en: But in the event, the contacts that exist between these two consuls turn out to be much more secure than the communication links between
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这两位执政官之间的联系比

sentences.en: Hasdrubal and Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 哈斯德鲁巴和汉尼拔之间的通讯联络要可靠得多。

sentences.en: So Hasdrubal obviously is desperate to rendezvous with his elder brother and find a point where they can kind of meet up and combine their forces.
sentences.zh: 哈斯德鲁巴显然急于与他的哥哥会合，寻找一个可以汇合并联合兵力的地方。

sentences.en: And so he inevitably, you know, who are you going to turn to when you want to deliver a message?
sentences.zh: 所以他不可避免地，你知道，当你想要传递信息时，你会求助于谁？

sentences.en: Obviously in Numidians.
sentences.zh: 显然是努米底亚人。

sentences.en: So he gets a bunch of Numidians, supplements them with a few Gauls, writes out a message.
sentences.zh: 所以他找了一群努米底亚人，补充了一些高卢人，写下了一条信息。

sentences.en: And this message is, meet in Umbria, and he sends the Numidians and Gauls off.
sentences.zh: 这条信息是：在翁布里亚会合，然后他把努米底亚人和高卢人派走了。

sentences.en: And why Umbria?
sentences.zh: 为什么是翁布里亚？

sentences.en: Well, this was the region where Hannibal had won at Lake Trasimene.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是汉尼拔在特拉西梅诺湖取得胜利的地区。

sentences.en: It's in northern Italy.
sentences.zh: 它在意大利北部。

sentences.en: It's on the way from the foothills of the Alps towards Rome.
sentences.zh: 它位于从阿尔卑斯山麓通往罗马的路上。

sentences.en: And this suggests that the Carthaginian plan was for the two brothers, once they had met up, to march directly on the capital and force the
sentences.zh: 这表明迦太基的计划是让两兄弟在会合后，直接进军首都，迫使

sentences.en: Romans to face them in battle.
sentences.zh: 罗马人与他们正面交战。

sentences.en: Because up to this point, the Romans, of course, had been avoiding meeting Hannibal in battle.
sentences.zh: 因为在此之前，罗马人当然一直在避免与汉尼拔正面交战。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, the aim is we will stake everything on a single throw.
sentences.zh: 我认为，目标就是我们将一切押在孤注一掷上。

sentences.en: But obviously for this to happen, Hasdrubal's message has to reach Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 但显然要实现这一点，哈斯德鲁巴的信息必须传达到汉尼拔手中。

sentences.en: And the problem is that it doesn't, because it falls into the hands of Nero, the beautifully groomed
sentences.zh: 问题是它没能传到，因为它落入了尼禄手中，那位仪表堂堂的

sentences.en: Claudian consul, whose job it is to bottle up Hannibal in the south.
sentences.zh: 克劳狄执政官，他的任务是在南方困住汉尼拔。

sentences.en: And when he gets this message and reads it, he reacts as Hannibal would have done in his sandals, with boldness and with an incredible display of initiative.
sentences.zh: 当他收到并读到这条信息时，他做出了汉尼拔会做出的反应，表现得极其大胆，展现了令人难以置信的主动性。

sentences.en: So what Nero does is to trick Hannibal into thinking that he is still with his legions.
sentences.zh: 所以尼禄所做的就是欺骗汉尼拔，让他以为自己还带着军团。

sentences.en: He does this while he is simultaneously siphoning off a very substantial body of infantry.
sentences.zh: 他在做这件事的同时，还在暗中抽调了一支相当庞大的步兵部队。

sentences.en: And he then marches with this body of infantry at incredible speed northwards towards where Salinator is refusing to have a wash.
sentences.zh: 随后，他率领这支步兵部队以惊人的速度向北进军，前往萨利纳托尔拒绝洗澡的地方。

sentences.en: And as he marches, he is joined along the way by enthusiastic volunteers.
sentences.zh: 在行军途中，不断有热情的志愿者加入他的队伍。

sentences.en: So that by the time he reaches Salinator's camp on the 22nd of June, you know, he is bringing a very, very large body of men to join the six legions under Salinator's camp.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他在6月22日抵达萨利纳托尔的营地时，他带来了一支非常非常庞大的军队，与萨利纳托尔营地下的六个军团汇合。

sentences.en: And Hasdrubal has no idea at all that Nero has arrived until he hears in the morning, not the one blast of the trumpet that signals the presence of a consul, but two.
sentences.zh: 哈斯德鲁巴根本不知道尼禄已经抵达，直到那天早上他听到的不是象征执政官到来的那一声号角，而是两声。

sentences.en: And this indicates to him that there are two consuls with their armies facing him.
sentences.zh: 这向他表明，有两位执政官正率领各自的军队面对着他。

sentences.en: And you can imagine, I mean, his heart must have turned to ice.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，他的心一定凉了半截。

sentences.en: And so he thinks, oh God, this is terrible.
sentences.zh: 于是他心想，天哪，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: I can't, you know,
sentences.zh: 我不能，你知道的，

sentences.en: I'm going to be annihilated if I meet them.
sentences.zh: 如果我与他们交战，我会被彻底消灭。

sentences.en: And so he tries to withdraw, but he has a problem because his line of retreat is blocked by a river called the Metaurus.
sentences.zh: 于是他试图撤退，但他遇到了麻烦，因为他的撤退路线被梅陶鲁斯河挡住了。

sentences.en: And so he leads his men, they're kind of stumbling through the marshy banks of the Metaurus trying to find a fording place.
sentences.zh: 于是他带领部下，在梅陶鲁斯河泥泞的河岸上跌跌撞撞地寻找渡口。

sentences.en: And as they're doing this, they're set upon by the Romans and the battle is lost almost before it had begun.
sentences.zh: 就在他们这样做的时候，罗马人发起了进攻，这场战斗几乎在开始之前就已经输了。

sentences.en: Now it's true that the defeat was actually, I mean, it wasn't total.
sentences.zh: 诚然，这次失败其实，我是说，并不是彻底的毁灭。

sentences.en: Had Hasdrubal survived, had he been able to lead his men and cross the Metaurus and withdraw to the foothills of the Alps?
sentences.zh: 如果哈斯德鲁巴活了下来，如果他能带领部下渡过梅陶鲁斯河并撤退到阿尔卑斯山的山脚下呢？

sentences.en: I mean, he would entirely have been able to carry on the fight, but Hasdrubal dies in the thick of the fighting.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他完全有能力继续战斗，但哈斯德鲁巴死在了激战之中。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very brave, but I think he's a bit stupid to have done that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他非常勇敢，但我认为他这样做有点愚蠢。

sentences.en: Polybius says that he displayed in his death a fortitude and an ability of spirit worthy of his family name.
sentences.zh: 波利比乌斯说，他在临死前展现出的坚毅和精神力量，配得上他的家族名声。

sentences.en: But I don't think he displayed the shrewdness that Hannibal would have done in his situation because his plunging
sentences.zh: 但我认为他没有展现出汉尼拔在那种情况下会有的精明，因为他冲进

sentences.en: into the thick of the melee essentially dooms his army and therefore in the long run, as we will see, dooms Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 混战中心的行为本质上注定了他的军队会失败，因此从长远来看，正如我们将要看到的，也注定了汉尼拔的失败。

sentences.en: Now, when Hannibal had defeated the Romans at Cannae, they had killed one of the commanders, a guy called Aemilius Paulus.
sentences.zh: 当汉尼拔在坎尼击败罗马人时，他们杀死了其中一位指挥官，一个叫埃米利乌斯·保卢斯的人。

sentences.en: And Hannibal had shown the corpse of Paulus great respect.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔对保卢斯的尸体表现出了极大的尊重。

sentences.en: You know, he had not desecrated it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他没有亵渎它。

sentences.en: Nero and Salinator, when they find the body of Hasdrubal, do not show it a matching respect.
sentences.zh: 尼禄和萨利纳托尔在发现哈斯德鲁巴的尸体时，并没有表现出同样的尊重。

sentences.en: They cut off its head and they put Hasdrubal's head into a sack and then they give it to a horseman.
sentences.zh: 他们砍下了他的头，把哈斯德鲁巴的头装进一个袋子里，然后交给了一名骑兵。

sentences.en: And this horseman gallops southwards, reaches the outposts that surround Hannibal's camp, gallops up to one of these outposts, hurls the sack at the feet of
sentences.zh: 这名骑兵向南疾驰，到达了包围汉尼拔营地的哨所，冲到其中一个哨所前，把袋子扔在

sentences.en: Hannibal's guards in this outpost, turns, wheels and gallops away.
sentences.zh: 这个哨所里汉尼拔卫兵的脚下，然后转身、调头，飞驰而去。

sentences.en: And the sack is brought to Hannibal and Hannibal opens it and he pulls out the severed head of his brother.
sentences.zh: 袋子被带到了汉尼拔面前，汉尼拔打开袋子，取出了他兄弟那颗被砍下的头颅。

sentences.en: And we are told that he mourns his brother, but that staring into his dead brother's features, he also mourns his city.
sentences.zh: 据说他为兄弟哀悼，但当他凝视着死去的兄弟的面容时，他也为自己的城市感到悲哀。

sentences.en: And he cries out, we are told, now at last, I see the doom of Carthage plain.
sentences.zh: 据说他大喊道：现在，我终于看清了迦太基的末日。

sentences.en: This is the moment, I think, when Hannibal knows that probably the game is up.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这就是汉尼拔意识到大势已去的那一刻。

sentences.en: But not quite up.
sentences.zh: 但还不完全是。

sentences.en: Because, OK, he's not going to be getting reinforcements from Iberia.
sentences.zh: 因为，好吧，他不会再得到来自伊比利亚的增援了。

sentences.en: But the
sentences.zh: 但是

sentences.en: Romans are still, they're so wary of his enormous military reputation, they don't confront him in open battle.
sentences.zh: 罗马人仍然对他巨大的军事声望心存忌惮，他们不敢在公开战场上与他正面交锋。

sentences.en: So he actually now heads even further south, doesn't he, away from Rome, into the heel of
sentences.zh: 所以他现在实际上向更南边进发了，不是吗？远离罗马，进入意大利的脚后跟，

sentences.en: Italy, into what's called Brutium.
sentences.zh: 进入所谓的布鲁提乌姆地区。

sentences.en: And that's the area that he can hold most easily if the Romans are coming after him.
sentences.zh: 如果罗马人追击他，那是他最容易防守的地区。

sentences.en: He also, of course, does have a brother left.
sentences.zh: 当然，他还有一个兄弟在世。

sentences.en: He has Mago back in Spain.
sentences.zh: 他在西班牙还有马戈。

sentences.en: And if you're Hannibal, you are probably thinking, well, if Mago can defeat Scipio in Spain, if he can win
sentences.zh: 如果你是汉尼拔，你可能会想，如果马戈能在西班牙击败西庇阿，如果他能赢

sentences.en: back the loyalty of the Iberians, who've gone over to the Romans, if, who knows, maybe Mago can recapture New Carthage.
sentences.zh: 回那些投靠罗马人的伊比利亚人的忠诚，如果，谁知道呢，也许马戈能收复新迦太基。

sentences.en: Maybe he can raise a new army.
sentences.zh: 也许他能组建一支新军队。

sentences.en: Maybe he can send reinforcements to Italy.
sentences.zh: 也许他能向意大利派遣增援部队。

sentences.en: So quite a lot of ifs.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多“如果”。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a lot of ifs in any war.
sentences.zh: 是的，任何战争中都有很多“如果”。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, not all of these ifs work out to Hannibal's advantage, do they?
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，并非所有这些“如果”都对汉尼拔有利，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we said Mago is a very good general.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们说过马戈是一位非常优秀的将军。

sentences.en: He's very, very dashing and very competent.
sentences.zh: 他非常、非常果敢且非常有能力。

sentences.en: I mean, his problem is, for the first time, he is facing a Roman general who essentially is as able and inventive as Hannibal himself.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他的问题在于，他第一次面对一位本质上和汉尼拔一样有能力、有创造力的罗马将军。

sentences.en: And Scipio essentially is going to crush all Hannibal's hopes because he is going to demolish the Carthaginian Empire in Spain.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿基本上要粉碎汉尼拔所有的希望，因为他要摧毁迦太基在西班牙的帝国。

sentences.en: So in the spring of 206, he has cornered Mago at a place called Ilippo, which is north of what's now
sentences.zh: 所以在公元前206年的春天，他在一个叫伊利帕的地方把马戈逼入了绝境，那里在现在塞维利亚的北边。

sentences.en: Seville.
sentences.zh: 塞维利亚。

sentences.en: And they meet in battle.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里交战。

sentences.en: And alongside Mago is Masanissa, who's no longer a prince by this point, but a king because his father died a few months before.
sentences.zh: 马戈身边是马西尼萨，此时他已不再是王子，而是一位国王，因为他的父亲几个月前去世了。

sentences.en: And so he is now the leader of this kind of federation of Numidian tribes called the Mysulians.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在是那个被称为马苏里安人的努米底亚部落联盟的领袖。

sentences.en: So he is, you know, I mean, he's now a very, very big player for the Carthaginians, not just a great commander, but an allied king.
sentences.zh: 所以他，你知道，我是说，他现在对迦太基人来说是一个非常、非常重要的角色，不仅是一位伟大的指挥官，还是一位盟友国王。

sentences.en: And so Mago and
sentences.zh: 所以马戈和

sentences.en: Masanissa, I mean, they must have been hopeful that they would be able to defeat Scipio.
sentences.zh: 马西尼萨，我是说，他们一定曾满怀希望，认为自己能够击败西庇阿。

sentences.en: Mago would back himself.
sentences.zh: 马戈对自己很有信心。

sentences.en: He knows that the Romans have always been kind of powerless against the Numidians.
sentences.zh: 他知道罗马人一直以来对努米底亚人束手无策。

sentences.en: But no, it doesn't turn out at all.
sentences.zh: 但并没有，结果完全不是那样。

sentences.en: Actually, they find the battle that Scipio now forces on them, I mean, to put it mildly, a very, very bruising experience.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他们发现西庇阿强加给他们的这场战斗，委婉地说，是一次非常、非常惨痛的经历。

sentences.en: So first, Masanissa's Numidian horsemen, you know, these great, great cavalrymen, they're swatted aside by Scipio's cavalry.
sentences.zh: 首先，马西尼萨的努米底亚骑兵，你知道，这些伟大的、伟大的骑兵，被西庇阿的骑兵击溃了。

sentences.en: So people will remember that when Scipio captured New Carthage, he'd insisted on lots of drill, lots of practice.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会记得，当西庇阿攻占新迦太基时，他坚持进行了大量的演练和练习。

sentences.en: And this is now paying off, because essentially, he has transformed his cavalry into the best horseman that Rome has ever had.
sentences.zh: 现在这得到了回报，因为从本质上讲，他已经把他的骑兵变成了罗马有史以来最优秀的骑兵。

sentences.en: And they just, you know, they swat Masanissa and his horsemen aside.
sentences.zh: 他们只是，你知道，他们把马西尼萨和他的骑兵击溃了。

sentences.en: There's then a stalemate, but one day passes, another day passes, another day passes.
sentences.zh: 随后陷入了僵局，但一天过去了，又一天过去了，再一天过去了。

sentences.en: Mago's concentration drops.
sentences.zh: 马戈的注意力下降了。

sentences.en: And this is the moment when Scipio attacks.
sentences.zh: 这就是西庇阿发起进攻的时刻。

sentences.en: And Mago, who we said had been, you know, he's a veteran of Cannae, he'd stood in the lines alongside Hannibal, he now finds
sentences.zh: 而我们说过是坎尼之战老兵的马戈，曾与汉尼拔并肩作战的马戈，现在发现

sentences.en: that he is the one who is being outflanked and enveloped by a smaller army.
sentences.zh: 自己竟然被一支规模较小的军队包抄和包围了。

sentences.en: And Scipio has the winning of the battle.
sentences.zh: 西庇阿赢得了这场战斗。

sentences.en: And although both Mago and Masanissa are able to escape the slaughter,
sentences.zh: 尽管马戈和马西尼萨都得以从屠杀中逃脱，

sentences.en: Mago's army, which was the last effective force left him in Iberia, is wiped out.
sentences.zh: 但马戈的军队，也就是他在伊比利亚剩下的最后的一支有效力量，被全歼了。

sentences.en: I mean, to give
sentences.zh: 我是说，给

sentences.en: Mago credit, he still doesn't give up.
sentences.zh: 马戈记上一功，他仍然没有放弃。

sentences.en: So first of all, he tries to do a Scipio and launch an attack on New Carthage.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，他试图效仿西庇阿，对新迦太基发动进攻。

sentences.en: In his case, it doesn't work, he gets beaten off.
sentences.zh: 就他而言，这没起作用，他被击退了。

sentences.en: He then sails away, he founds a new naval base on the island of Mallorca, in the Balearics, which to this day bears his name,
sentences.zh: 然后他扬帆远航，在巴利阿里群岛的马略卡岛上建立了一个新的海军基地，至今仍以他的名字命名，

sentences.en: Mahon.
sentences.zh: 马翁。

sentences.en: And this apparently is where mayonnaise was invented.
sentences.zh: 据说这就是蛋黄酱的发明地。

sentences.en: So in a way, mayonnaise is named after
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，蛋黄酱是以

sentences.en: Mago.
sentences.zh: 马戈命名的。

sentences.en: I think it's the only popular condiment.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是唯一受欢迎的调味品。

sentences.en: It's a condiment, really?
sentences.zh: 它真的是调味品吗？

sentences.en: I was just thinking, is it a condiment?
sentences.zh: 我刚才在想，它算调味品吗？

sentences.en: Well, if it's not a condiment, I don't know what it is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果它不是调味品，我不知道它是什么。

sentences.en: It's not a sauce, is it?
sentences.zh: 它不是酱汁，对吧？

sentences.en: It can be used as both, but I think mayonnaise is more than, it contains multitudes.
sentences.zh: 它两者都可以用，但我认为蛋黄酱不仅仅是那样，它包含了很多东西。

sentences.en: It's something you'd have in your fridge.
sentences.zh: 它是你会放在冰箱里的东西。

sentences.en: And it's probably the only thing you'd have in a fridge that's named after a Carthaginian general.
sentences.zh: 而且它可能是你冰箱里唯一以迦太基将军命名的东西。

sentences.en: So it's kind of interesting detail.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个很有趣的细节。

sentences.en: Anyway, so he's still on the scene.
sentences.zh: 总之，他仍然活跃在舞台上。

sentences.en: And then in 205, he launches a very ambitious invasion of northern Italy.
sentences.zh: 然后在公元前205年，他发动了一场雄心勃勃的入侵意大利北部的行动。

sentences.en: You know, he takes ships, he takes men.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他带了船，带了人。

sentences.en: He captures Genoa.
sentences.zh: 他占领了热那亚。

sentences.en: So that's quite a feat.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一项了不起的壮举。

sentences.en: And he manages to hold out there against the Romans for three years.
sentences.zh: 他设法在那里抵御了罗马人三年。

sentences.en: There's an indecisive battle.
sentences.zh: 发生了一场不分胜负的战斗。

sentences.en: He gets wounded.
sentences.zh: 他受伤了。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians summon him back to his home city.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人召他回故乡。

sentences.en: And on the trip, he dies.
sentences.zh: 在回程途中，他去世了。

sentences.en: So an energetic end.
sentences.zh: 所以是一个充满活力的结局。

sentences.en: But that's the end of Mago.
sentences.zh: 但马戈的故事到此结束了。

sentences.en: And what about Masanissa?
sentences.zh: 那么马西尼萨呢？

sentences.en: Well, for him, the days of fighting the
sentences.zh: 嗯，对他来说，与

sentences.en: Romans are now over because this is the moment in the wake of Scipio's great victory at Ilippa that he makes contact with the Roman victor.
sentences.zh: 罗马人作战的日子现在结束了，因为就在西庇阿在伊利帕取得伟大胜利之后，他与这位罗马胜利者取得了联系。

sentences.en: And the result is the meeting described by Livy, the homoerotic summit with which we began this episode.
sentences.zh: 结果就是李维所描述的那次会面，也就是我们本集开头提到的那场同性恋色彩浓厚的峰会。

sentences.en: Because Masanissa is basically like the
sentences.zh: 因为马西尼萨基本上就像

sentences.en: Iberians.
sentences.zh: 伊比利亚人一样。

sentences.en: I mean, he has no interest in fighting for a losing side.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他对为失败的一方作战毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: And it's very clear to him by this point that the Carthaginians have no future whatsoever in Iberia.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，此时非常清楚，迦太基人在伊比利亚没有任何未来。

sentences.en: And so he contacts Scipio.
sentences.zh: 于是他联系了西庇阿。

sentences.en: They get on tremendously well.
sentences.zh: 他们相处得非常好。

sentences.en: And with Scipio's blessing, he returns to Africa there to secure his rule as king because this other rival king, Sifax, is still on the scene.
sentences.zh: 在西庇阿的祝福下，他回到了非洲，以巩固他作为国王的统治，因为另一个竞争对手国王西法克斯仍然在场。

sentences.en: So he needs to sort that out.
sentences.zh: 所以他需要解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And Scipio, by sending Masanissa, now a Roman ally, to Africa, is obviously looking ahead
sentences.zh: 而西庇阿通过派遣现在已成为罗马盟友的马西尼萨前往非洲，显然是在未雨绸缪，

sentences.en: because the only way that the war ultimately can be ended is if the Romans can take the war to Carthage itself.
sentences.zh: 因为战争最终结束的唯一途径是罗马人能把战争带到迦太基本土。

sentences.en: And in late 206, Scipio returns to Rome, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 在公元前206年底，西庇阿回到了罗马，不是吗？

sentences.en: And he is now a real star.
sentences.zh: 他现在是一位真正的明星。

sentences.en: He's had tremendous achievements in the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 他在战场上取得了巨大的成就。

sentences.en: He's glamorous.
sentences.zh: 他魅力四射。

sentences.en: He's charismatic.
sentences.zh: 他很有个人魅力。

sentences.en: He's got his exciting long hair.
sentences.zh: 他留着那头令人兴奋的长发。

sentences.en: And he is determined to win the prize that will confirm all this, which is the consulship.
sentences.zh: 他决心赢得能证实这一切的奖赏，那就是执政官职位。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Even though he's only 30 and legally you have to be 40 to become a consul.
sentences.zh: 尽管他只有30岁，而法律规定必须年满40岁才能成为执政官。

sentences.en: So he gets the consulship and he has allocated province, a very rich, strategically important province that will be his once he has finished his consulship.
sentences.zh: 所以他获得了执政官职位，并被分配了一个行省，一个非常富裕、具有战略重要性的行省，一旦他结束执政官任期，那将属于他。

sentences.en: And that is Sicily.
sentences.zh: 那就是西西里岛。

sentences.en: And the command in Sicily comes not just with boots on the ground, i.e. the legions, but it comes with a fleet of 30 warships.
sentences.zh: 西西里岛的指挥权不仅带来了地面部队，即军团，还带来了一支由30艘战舰组成的舰队。

sentences.en: So this is what he needs.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他所需要的。

sentences.en: And on top of that, Dominic, crucially, he is given permission by the Senate, and I quote, to cross to Africa if he judged it to be in the interests of the Republic.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，多米尼克，关键在于，他获得了元老院的许可，引用原文，“如果他认为符合共和国的利益，可以跨海前往非洲”。

sentences.en: But the big question,
sentences.zh: 但最大的问题是，

sentences.en: will Scipio judge it to be in the interests of the Republic, to cross the sea, to invade Africa, and to attack the Carthaginians in their very backyard?
sentences.zh: 西庇阿会认为跨海前往非洲、入侵非洲并攻击迦太基人的大本营符合共和国的利益吗？

sentences.en: There is only one way to find out.
sentences.zh: 只有一个办法可以知道。

sentences.en: So if you're a member of the Rest is History Club, and you want to find out whether Scipio will indeed cross to Africa and launch the final
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是“历史就是一切”俱乐部的成员，并且想知道西庇阿是否真的会跨海前往非洲并对迦太基人发动最后的

sentences.en: assault on the Carthaginians, you can find out right now, because if you're a member of that club,
sentences.zh: 攻击，你现在就可以知道，因为如果你是该俱乐部的成员，

sentences.en: you can hear episode three, and indeed episode four of this series, instantaneously.
sentences.zh: 你可以立即收听本系列的第三集，甚至是第四集。

sentences.en: If you're not a member of the club, you'll have to wait, gnawing at your nails like Gordon Brown in the aftermath of the financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是俱乐部的成员，你就得等着，像金融危机后的戈登·布朗一样咬着指甲等待。

sentences.en: But either way, the Punic Wars will continue and they will reach a devastating, heart-stopping climax.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，布匿战争将继续下去，并将达到一个毁灭性的、令人心跳停止的高潮。

sentences.en: Tom, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Goodbye, everybody.
sentences.zh: 再见，各位。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Okay, so here's a glimpse of what's to come.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这里是即将发生的事情的预告。

sentences.en: If it sparks something unexplainable, then you can join us every Tuesday and Thursday for new episodes of The Rest is Science, and we'll figure it out together.
sentences.zh: 如果它激发了某种无法解释的东西，那么你可以每周二和周四加入我们，收听《科学就是一切》的新剧集，我们将一起弄清楚它。

sentences.en: You mentioned earlier that a cup of water is like a rock smoothie, right?
sentences.zh: 你之前提到一杯水就像岩石冰沙，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you've got rocks dissolved in it, magnesium and calcium.
sentences.zh: 因为里面溶解了岩石，镁和钙。

sentences.en: I would go a step further, though, and say that a glass of water is actually just a glass of lava.
sentences.zh: 不过，我会更进一步，说一杯水实际上只是一杯熔岩。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Because I've talked about this before, and I bring it up whenever I can.
sentences.zh: 因为我之前谈过这个，而且只要有机会我就会提。

sentences.en: Ice is a rock.
sentences.zh: 冰是一种岩石。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Because, well, hold on.
sentences.zh: 因为，嗯，等等。

sentences.en: Ice is a mineral.
sentences.zh: 冰是一种矿物。

sentences.en: Because a mineral is just an inorganic material that is solid and has a definite crystal structure, which ice does.
sentences.zh: 因为矿物就是一种无机固体，且具有确定的晶体结构，而冰恰好符合这些条件。

sentences.en: Water is important for life, but it's inorganic, actually.
sentences.zh: 水对生命很重要，但实际上它是无机物。

sentences.en: It would exist here whether there was life or not.
sentences.zh: 无论有没有生命存在，它都会存在于这里。

sentences.en: And what that then means is that a cube of ice is made of a mineral.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一块冰是由矿物组成的。

sentences.en: So it's a monomineralic rock.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一种单矿物岩。

sentences.en: So melted ice is molten rock.
sentences.zh: 所以融化的冰就是熔岩。

sentences.en: Lava.
sentences.zh: 岩浆。

sentences.en: So water is lava.
sentences.zh: 所以水就是岩浆。

sentences.en: I'm here for this.
sentences.zh: 我支持这个说法。

sentences.en: And this is not a joke.
sentences.zh: 而且这不是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: Ice won the mineral cup back in 2015, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我相信冰在2015年赢得了矿物杯。

sentences.en: Like some geologists all voted on their favorite mineral, and ice finally got the recognition it deserves.
sentences.zh: 就像一些地质学家投票选出他们最喜欢的矿物，冰终于得到了它应得的认可。

sentences.en: Got the prize.
sentences.zh: 拿到了奖项。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, sure.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当然。

sentences.en: I'm happy with that classification.
sentences.zh: 我对这个分类很满意。

sentences.en: If the rock people say it so, then I'm happy with it.
sentences.zh: 如果研究岩石的人都这么说，那我就没意见。
